cases.title: Block mapping of scalars
cases.paragraph: A mapping node represents an association of key/value pairs.

cases.title: Block sequence
cases.paragraph: A sequence node represents an ordered series of nodes.

cases.title: Flow mapping and sequence (JSON-like)
cases.paragraph: Flow collections use explicit indicators similar to JSON.

cases.title: Plain scalar yes is a boolean in YAML 1.1
cases.paragraph: YAML 1.1 resolves y|Y|yes|Yes|YES|n|N|no|No|NO|true|True|TRUE|false|False|FALSE|on|On|ON|off|Off|OFF to booleans.

cases.title: Plain scalar off is a boolean in YAML 1.1
cases.paragraph: off is a canonical boolean false in the YAML 1.1 type repository.

cases.title: Tilde is null
cases.paragraph: A tilde (~) or the empty scalar may resolve to null.

cases.title: Anchor and alias reuse a node
cases.paragraph: An alias node refers to the most recent node having the same anchor.

cases.title: Quoted yes remains a string
cases.paragraph: Quoted scalars are not subject to implicit type resolution.

cases.title: Sexagesimal integers exist in YAML 1.1
cases.paragraph: YAML 1.1 integers include base-60 sexagesimal values such as 1:2 (62).
cases.notes: YAML 1.2 removed sexagesimal. PyYAML 1.1 loaders typically produce 62.

cases.title: Tab characters must not be used for indentation
cases.paragraph: In YAML block styles, indentation is defined by space characters. Tab characters must not be used.

cases.title: Unterminated quoted scalar is an error
cases.paragraph: A double-quoted scalar must be closed by a matching quotation mark.
